- **`anchored-edit` refuses new text in which a line matches the `read_lines` anchor prefix shape (bob#223).** `edit_lines`, `insert_after` and `write_file` refuse text in which any line starts with the rendered anchor shape (`L<n>#<h> ` with `<h>` 8 lowercase hex characters), and write nothing. The guard matches the shape only, so it refuses a prefix copied from a `read_lines` result and genuine content that begins the same way alike. When the call's earlier checks pass, the refusal names the tool, the first matching line number and the remedy (strip the prefixes if the text was copied; report BLOCKED and name the file if its real content needs such a line); a call that an earlier check refuses, such as one with a stale anchor or fingerprint or one on a file whose rewrite budget already tripped, gets that refusal instead. A new call's own charge against the rewrite budget runs after the guard, so an `edit_lines` call that would newly exceed the limit and has a matching line gets the prefix refusal. No tool argument and no configuration turns the guard off; an argument a tool does not declare is ignored and never changes the result. There is deliberately no escape hatch, because no channel the agent cannot write exists for one yet: content whose lines genuinely begin with that shape has to be written outside these tools. Rendering has one definition (`ANCHOR_FORMAT` in `core.ts`); the guard's matcher, like the anchor parser's, is a literal regex pinned to it by a contract test, which checks each literal's source against `ANCHOR_FORMAT` and both literals against real `read_lines` output for lines 1, 9, 10 and 99999: the guard's matcher matches exactly each rendered prefix and nothing else there, and the parser reads each rendered token back. (`test/capabilities/anchored-edit/anchor-prefix.test.ts`)
